post.caption: Diamond deals still close on one word. Dealers seal a sale with a handshake and the word mazal. The full phrase is mazal u'bracha, which means luck and blessing. Once those words are said, nothing goes on paper. The same custom is used in Antwerp and in New York. What backs the deal is reputation, because word spreads fast. A diamond often travels in a small folded paper packet. Billions of dollars in diamonds change hands on those words. New York's Diamond Dealers Club settles disputes by its own arbitration. That club began in 1931 with twelve people at its first meeting.
